best_for: Home-lab owners and small teams who want to reach their own machines from anywhere without opening router ports or running a VPN server.
description:
Tailscale is the app for Tailscale Inc.'s private network service, which the company says 60,000 businesses use. The same app is offered for home use, with your own laptop, phone and servers on one private network.

Each device gets a short, readable name through MagicDNS, so you type nas instead of an IP address. You can pick one machine as an exit node and send all your traffic through it, much like a privacy VPN. Taildrop sends large files between your devices. Funnel shares a folder or service on the public internet over HTTPS, and node sharing lets you give one machine to a friend on another Tailscale network.

points.title: A private network without port forwarding
points.text: Tailscale links your devices into one WireGuard-based mesh, so a laptop on hotel Wi-Fi can reach a home NAS directly. You install the app and sign in; there is no server to set up.

points.title: Free for personal use
points.text: The Personal plan costs nothing for non-commercial use, with up to 6 users and unlimited user devices, 3 ACL groups and 50 tagged resources.

points.title: Business use is paid
points.text: Standard is $8 and Premium $18 per user per month, with Enterprise priced on request. Premium adds network flow logs, log streaming and advanced Tailscale SSH. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Sign-in goes through an identity provider
points.text: You sign up with a single sign-on account rather than a Tailscale password. A public email such as Gmail lands on Personal; a custom domain starts a 14-day Enterprise trial.

points.title: Core is open, the GUIs are not
points.text: The `tailscaled` daemon and `tailscale` CLI are BSD-3-Clause open source. The project says the GUI wrappers on non-open-source platforms are themselves closed.

points.title: Three ways to run it on a Mac
points.text: All need macOS 13 or later. The standalone package listed here is the one Tailscale recommends and needs no Apple ID. The App Store version cannot run `tailscale ssh`; the open source `tailscaled` has no GUI.

points.title: Windows 10 and later
points.text: The Windows client needs Windows 10 or Server 2016 or later, with x86, x64 and Arm64 builds and an MSI option. The Windows listing keeps 134 versions; macOS lists only the current release.
